neighbours.q: Why don't antibiotics work against viruses like the flu?
neighbours.label: medfacts
neighbours.reply:
Antibiotics are designed to target and kill bacteria. They work by interfering with the processes that bacteria need to survive and reproduce, such as attacking their cell walls or disrupting their ability to synthesize essential proteins.

Because of these fundamental differences, antibiotics are ineffective against viruses. They simply don't have the right targets to attack.
